transcript.text: Maya, before you proceed with the budget sign-off, I need to flag a key procurement condition. Yesterday I received the vendor's countersigned commercial schedule, which requires a 20% holdback on each implementation invoice until final acceptance. That means 20% of every invoice over the April-through-December implementation period will be retained and not paid out until final acceptance is achieved. I have not yet uploaded this schedule to the procurement repository, so I want to make sure everyone is aware of this holdback provision before we finalize the decision, as it will affect both the payment timing and the effective cash-flow profile of the project.

Thank you all for those important disclosures. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I make my decision:

1. From Jonas (accounting): $7.2M of the $12M is capitalizable; $4.8M is period expense.
2. From Leila (treasury): Only $9M can be funded before fiscal year-end while preserving the minimum cash floor; $3M must be funded after October 1.
3. From Grant (procurement): 20% holdback on each invoice until final acceptance, affecting payment timing and cash-flow profile.

All three conditions are material to the budget sign-off. The total $12M fits within the board-approved capital-plan envelope, so I can approve the project at that level. The capitalization split, the fiscal-year funding constraint, and the 20% vendor holdback will all be reflected in how we structure and track the project. I'll now record the formal decision.
